controls.name: Design and independent change review
controls.scope: Consequential designs, implementation, tests, delegation and exceptions.
controls.mechanism: Lead owns design/integration and verifies returned evidence; at most two workers use separate project-local worktrees and named disjoint paths, with shared runtime serialized; fresh-context review assesses contracts, risk and maintainability before acceptance. Apply S-CODE's outcome/reuse/platform-contract review across code/docs/workflow/controls: compare available capabilities and total cost against the overall objective, identify the residual project gap and configured platform guarantees, and reject unjustified duplication or disproportionate defense/recovery. Simplification and deletion are valid outcomes; deliberate accelerators/enablers are also valuable when expected repeated use, learning or future cost reduction warrants upfront effort. Review the relevant horizon, uncertainty, upkeep and reassessment trigger, without demanding immediate payoff or precise ROI. Routine choices add no evaluation report or approval layer. Before publication, inspect explicit Git author/committer identities and all new commit messages, including co-author trailers, under S-WORK. Use repository-local Git identity configuration. Before merging a PR whose Issue completion awaits merged-main validation, read gh pr view --json closingIssuesReferences, require an empty list and re-read after removing references. Prose negation is not a parser control; use GitHub computed data, no custom keyword parser. For source-dependent consequential claims, inspect executable predicates, caller cadence, units and defaults against actual outcomes; preserve mistaken rationale and which actions preceded correction. For changed native boundaries, compare synthetic category/action/row/transition assumptions with the pinned producer and retained visible frames; reject fictional UI labels used to arm control state. Reuse the existing regression/native lanes; do not infer native support from passing mocks. Development-first delivery places cohesive independent implementation/test/evidence review at integration/acceptance; consequential new boundaries retain earlier design/risk review. No routine readiness reviewer or per-action critic is added to ordinary development play. A complete unchanged unassisted development run can support its prospective functional outcome after exact-source checks/review; it is never retroactively relabeled held-out evidence. Review selection follows the decision-and-risk guidance in docs/project-management.md: choose applicable product/player/observer/architecture/research perspectives rather than every lens for every change. For consequential input/memory/learning/autonomy changes, verify the prior-document and research crosswalk required by S-ARCH, including conflicts and transfer limits. Independent proxy review does not establish real-user usability or semantic truth; no new automated semantic checker is added. For agent/memory changes, check S-ARCH's active/background ownership, automatic-versus-model feedback, attribution and revisable-advice boundaries; gameplay independence review checks that routine reasoning/curation does not depend on the engineering lead. This adds no per-action approval. At meaningful discussion/research/review/delivery checkpoints, check S-WORK action-item dispositions in the existing Issues/Project and applicable updates to authoritative principles, standards, controls and guidance; proposals and filed findings are not completed behavior. Apply S-ARCH/S-CODE generality and CDDA-class portability requirements: challenge task/menu-specific assumptions that obstruct ordinary input, inspect whole-loop recovery and changing-interface evidence, and separate shared responsibilities from game bindings. Record remaining coupling and actual portability limits. This is integration review, not a per-action gameplay gate. Check the documentation/GitHub authority split: retain purpose-specific capability/evidence summaries and design decisions, remove copied live fields, stale current claims and repeated attempt narratives, and keep detailed evidence in dated reports. This is manual integration review, not a duplicate-status tracker or semantic parser.

Identity configuration prevents inferred defaults but does not inspect file contents or prove a message, branch or remote ref contains no personal information; full-message inspection remains manual. Fixture realism is a manual source/evidence judgment; common tests cannot prove it. No automated check proves that discussion/research findings are fully represented in the backlog or correctly reconciled into authoritative artifacts. #191 owns the new generality/game-family constraint and remaining coupling. Source support for#176–178 and bounded learning004 evidence now exist; prior proposed-only wording describes the earlier baseline. No cross-game or unrestricted adversarial qualification exists.

controls.name: Rendered visual documentation
controls.scope: Mermaid sources and generated SVGs in docs/diagrams.
controls.mechanism: Pinned local Mermaid CLI renders every source in a headless project-local browser. Hash receipt covers sources, config, wrapper, package lock and tracked SVGs; title/description and root SVG ID are required. Explicit --write regenerates; normal checks leave tracked files unchanged.
controls.trigger: common command; source, renderer configuration or dependency changes require rendered review
controls.failure_response: Fix syntax or missing setup; regenerate stale output and inspect the rendered result. Never call a denied browser launch a passed check. Resolve semantic/readability findings through C-USABILITY/C-REVIEW.
controls.limitations: Receipt freshness is not cross-host byte equality or proof against deliberate falsification. Rendering and SVG metadata do not prove meaning, accessibility for every reader or readable layout. Human rendered inspection is required. Ubuntu 24.04 CI was exercised with a scoped runner Chrome sandbox profile; other Linux hosts remain unverified.
controls.enforcement: Common command fails on renderer errors, missing title/description/ID or changed input/output receipts; negative fixtures include a real parse failure. No global installation or automatic fetch.
controls.rationale: Required to keep user-facing visual explanations reviewable and synchronized.
